Subject: Privacy terms + annotated transfer map request

Hi Tessa / Marissa,

Thanks for the call earlier — HealTech is evaluating Redwood for inference on patient-facing features and we need a few artifacts to complete our privacy review before we start procurement:

- An annotated dataflow diagram showing where PII (PII = name, contact, PHI-adjacent identifiers) may touch Redwood systems and any subprocessors.
- Confirmation of encryption-in-transit and encryption-at-rest, plus whether KMS keys are customer-managed or Redwood-managed for the hosted setup.
- A short mapping of retention tiers for telemetry and model logs (what is retained, for how long, where).

We also flagged a couple of DPA items: subprocessors list (latest snapshot), and whether you have any cross-border transfer subcontractors (e.g., analytics vendors) that would trigger SCC/transfer annex requirements.

Can you send the annotated diagram and a one-page summary addressing the bullets above? If possible we’d like those by end of week — procurement is trying to lock timelines.

Appreciate it,
Samir

[HealTech — Security]
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Privacy terms + annotated transfer map request

Hi Samir —

Thanks for the clear list. I’ve attached an annotated dataflow (PDF) and a DPA answer summary (XLSX) that address each bullet. High-level answers up front:

- Dataflow: the annotated diagram shows three logical touch points where customer PII may be present: (1) ingestion API (prefix trimmed client-side), (2) short-lived inference KV cache during active request handling (ephemeral, cleared per session), and (3) optional telemetry aggregation buckets used for model perf but pseudonymized.
- Encryption: TLS 1.2+ in-transit by default; data at rest is AES-256. For Hosted customers keys are managed by Redwood KMS (we can offer BYOK for Dedicated/Private deployments; we offer KMS proxy options for RBAC-based customer key custody).
- Retention: telemetry (anonymized metrics) — 13 months; debug logs (redacted) — 90 days; request traces that include PII are retained 30 days by default and are purgeable on request (legal/POA). Details and override knobs are in the attached XLSX.
- Subprocessors: current snapshot included in sheet tab ‘Subprocessors_Sep2026’. Major ones: cloud provider compute, object storage provider, analytics vendor for aggregated metrics. We’ve called out cross-border subprocessors and the jurisdictions in the sheet.

Attachments: [Attachment: redwood-annotated-dataflow-v1.pdf (PDF, 428KB)], [Attachment: dpa-answer-summary-HEALTECH.xlsx (XLSX, 86KB)].

Two asks from our side to speed review: 1) can you confirm the specific PHI categories you consider in-scope (we marked defaults on the diagram but can tighten), and 2) do you require a customer-managed KMS for the hosted offering (if yes, we’ll propose Dedicated or Private options)?

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Tessa — thanks for the fast turnaround and the attachments. A couple of follow-ups after a quick pass:

- KMS: HealTech procurement prefers customer-managed KMS for Prod PHI use cases. We’re evaluating whether Dedicated meets our needs or if we need Private. Can you confirm whether Redwood can support a BYOK integration for the Hosted plan as an exception?

- Subprocessors: the spreadsheet lists an analytics vendor in EMEA. Can you confirm whether that vendor receives any raw request payloads or only aggregated telemetry? Also please confirm if any subprocessors have access to the KV cache or tracing data (we want explicit separation).

- Evidence: can you provide the latest SOC2 summary or a link to your compliance artefacts? Procurement wants the exhibit to attach to the PO.

If it’s easier I can hop on a 30-min call — available Thu afternoon.

Thanks,
Samir
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Aug 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: HealTech — privacy terms & annotated transfer map questions

Marissa / Jonas — forwarding Samir’s follow-ups above. Summary / proposed internal plan:

1) BYOK for Hosted: we don’t have a standard Hosted-BYOK path today. Options to propose: (A) Dedicated contract with BYOK add-on (fastest, already supported), (B) Private deployment (longer lead, supported), or (C) temporary exception for Hosted under an escrow/BLA arrangement — needs legal sign-off and a security risk assessment. Recommend we push Dedicated as the primary option and offer Private for customers requiring on-prem KMS.

2) Subprocessor access: analytics vendor receives only aggregated telemetry (no raw request payloads). KV cache and trace data live on ephemeral instances and are scoped to our serving cluster; no subprocessors have direct access. I propose we confirm this in writing and add a short export-control clause in the DPA appendix to be safe.

3) Evidence: attach SOC2 summary + compliance portal link (I’ll request the latest package from Security Ops). Procurement wants a bundle we can attach to the PO — I’ll coordinate with Legal for redaction if necessary.

Next steps I suggest: Jonas to confirm the exact wording we can share on subprocessors (one-liner plus pointer to sheet), Marissa to draft DPA appendix options (Dedicated/BYOK language), Tessa to pull SOC2 export and coordinate with Security Ops. Can we aim to have an internal draft by Monday morning?

— Tessa
